first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this after asking whether her friends should all fly over for the wedding. The intro promises 'asking friends to travel', which is exactly the conversation we're having at home, so I kept going. Sensible, polite tone, short paragraphs, easy to read on the iPad.

journey.quote: For a wedding abroad, ask attendants early and talk openly about travel, time off and who covers what before anyone books.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the line I'd have written myself. 'Who covers what' is the question nobody in our family wants to raise first.

journey.quote: At a Roman wedding, friends and clients of both families gathered in the house of the bride's father.
journey.reaction: Interesting enough, but Athens, Rome and the word history take a while before anything I can act on. I'd skim this on a second read.

journey.section: 3. Queen Victoria's bridesmaids and royal attendants
journey.quote: A long train or cathedral veil needs one or two named attendants, briefed and rehearsed on the actual aisle, steps and turns of your ceremony venue.
journey.reaction: I like that it turns the history into something practical. Named people, rehearsed. That's how I'd want it run.

journey.section: 6. How many bridesmaids should you have?
journey.quote: At a destination wedding, every attendant is a guest making a real commitment.
journey.reaction: Yes. And somebody pays for that commitment. Glad it's said plainly rather than glossed over.

journey.section: 7. What bridesmaids and the maid of honour do, before and on the day
journey.quote: For a playful take, see [a peek inside a celebrity bridesmaid kit](/trending/whats-inside-rei-germars-bridesmaid-kit).
journey.reaction: I don't know who that is and I don't need to. It's the only spot where the page drifts towards social media chatter.

journey.quote: Who covers flights and accommodation, and is that the same for every attendant?
journey.reaction: This is the list I'll print out. It treats the money questions as normal, not awkward. I'd only add that whoever is actually paying, often us parents, should be in that conversation too.

journey.quote: Each attendant should tell their insurer about any pre-existing health conditions.
journey.reaction: Practical and sensible. One of the bridesmaids has a heart condition, so I'll pass this on.

journey.quote: Name one person the venue team can reach about the party's timings.
journey.reaction: One contact, named. That's the kind of order I want. Though it doesn't tell me who I ring if something goes wrong overnight their time.

journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Australian dollars and my own time zone. That answers two of my first questions before I've asked them.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing, before anything starts. Good. I'd still want a phone call before we pay a cent, and nothing here says deposits to overseas suppliers are protected.

unanswered_questions: Are deposits paid to overseas venues and suppliers protected, and who is responsible if a supplier lets us down?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day overseas, at 2am their time?
Is the first step a phone conversation with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked?
Is it usual for the bride's family to cover the attendants' travel, or do the attendants usually pay their own way to a wedding abroad?

turn_offs_found.quote: For a playful take, see [a peek inside a celebrity bridesmaid kit](/trending/whats-inside-rei-germars-bridesmaid-kit).
turn_offs_found.why: It reads as influencer content in an otherwise grown-up, practical article. It's one of my listed turn-offs (trendy, influencer tone), and it makes the brand feel briefly less serious about the money and responsibility questions I care about.

would_share_with: My husband, with section 9 marked, especially 'Questions to talk through together' and the travel insurance lines
My daughter, so she raises who covers flights and outfits with her bridesmaids before anyone books

cta_reaction.quote: You will work with one Wedded Advisor, your single point of contact from the first conversation to the wedding day.
cta_reaction.why: One named person, AUD quotes and the fee in writing are exactly what I look for. But this is an article about bridesmaids, so I'd click when my daughter is ready, and only if I knew a real person would ring before anything is paid.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, say plainly that the first step is a phone conversation with the advisor, before anything is booked.
In section 9 'Questions to talk through together', add a line that whoever is funding the wedding (often parents) should be part of the 'who covers what' conversation.
Drop or replace the celebrity bridesmaid kit link in section 7 with something practical, and tighten section 2 slightly so readers reach the destination advice sooner.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title and deferred business details not raised as must-fix; no sourcing lines requested; no prices requested

open_questions.question: Deposit protection, on-the-day emergency contact and 'phone call first' remain this persona's trust gaps, but business details are deferred. Treat as nice-to-have?

The question about who customarily covers attendants' travel is about custom and responsibility, not prices, so it fits the no-prices rule.
